sources.title: Jiří Lebl, Tasty Bits of Several Complex Variables: A Whirlwind Tour of the Subject, version 4.4
sources.locator: Chapter 1, §1.1, Theorem 1.1.4, printed pp. 15–16; §1.2, printed pp. 20–23; Chapter 2, §2.5; Chapter 4, §4.4, Lemma 4.4.7 and Theorem 4.4.5, printed pp. 142–145.

contents.result: Use the Cauchy and one-variable Laurent methods as background; Lebl's mixed several-variable Laurent expansion in Exercise 1.2.4 is only an exercise, so the item supplies the full coefficient construction and convergence proof.

The local Dolbeault lemma is treated in §4.4. The q=1 vector-valued reduction in Theorem 4.4.5 refers to Exercise 4.4.6, so this item uses its inspected local supplier instead of treating that exercise as proved.
Theorem 4.4.5 supplies local Dolbeault context; its global projective calculation is completed locally by the coefficient contraction.
One-variable Laurent expansion and normal-convergence methods inform the separately proved degree-weighted projective coefficient calculation.

sources.title: MIT OpenCourseWare 18.117 Topics in Several Complex Variables, Spring 2005, lecture notes prepared by Jonathan Campbell
sources.locator: Lectures 4, 7–9 and 11, PDF pp. 9–12, 18–23 and 23–25: local Dolbeault exactness, the projective atlas, sheaf/Čech cohomology, and Čech–Dolbeault comparison. The comparison proof is presented as a sketch and invokes the pseudoconvex Dolbeault theorem without proving it; it is contextual only. The chart map divides by the chosen homogeneous coordinate, so the standard chart condition is nonzero in that coordinate despite an apparent transcription error in the displayed condition.

contents.result: The notes define holomorphic line bundles by transition-function cocycles; the local item specializes these conventions to the projective coordinate transitions and checks the cocycle.
The notes fix the standard projective atlas and the ordered Čech nerve; the detailed analytic coefficient contraction and its convergence are proved locally.
The notes give an independent outline of the projective and Dolbeault comparison framework, not a complete proof of the present supplier interfaces.

sources.title: R. Dervan, lectures; Qiangru Kuang, notes, University of Cambridge Mathematics Tripos Part III, Complex Manifolds, Lent 2019
sources.locator: §3.1–3.2 and §4.4–4.5, printed pp. 9–11 and 23–26; §5, printed pp. 27–29. The Dolbeault theorem proof uses the local ∂-Poincaré lemma and smooth-sheaf acyclicity; Theorem 4.4 proves Čech comparison under acyclic-intersection hypotheses; the line-bundle and transition-function definitions are in §5. Its remark treats polydisc intersections, so it does not prove acyclicity of the projective intersections C^a×(C*)^b.

contents.result: The notes define holomorphic line bundles by transition-function cocycles; the local item specializes these conventions to the projective coordinate transitions and checks the cocycle.
The acyclic-cover comparison hypothesis and standard line-bundle language are used as independent checks; the required C^a×(C*)^b acyclicity is supplied by the local proof.
Theorem 4.3 gives the Dolbeault/sheaf comparison by an exact resolution and acyclic smooth-form sheaves; the local proof records the actual bundle-valued hypotheses.

sources.title: Jean-Pierre Serre, Géométrie algébrique et géométrie analytique, Annales de l'Institut Fourier 6 (1956), 1–42
sources.locator: §13, Lemma 4 and footnote 4, printed pp. 20–21. Lemma 4 establishes the comparison for the structure sheaf in Serre's GAGA proof; footnote 4 only mentions an unpublished Laurent-series computation by J. Frenkel and gives no argument.

contents.result: The source is retained as the planned historical reference, but its footnote is not evidence for the Laurent contraction.
The source's GAGA argument is not invoked; its footnote explicitly leaves the direct Laurent calculation unpublished.
The P2 contraction is proved locally and does not rely on the footnote.
The negative-twist computation is proved directly in the local Čech complex.
